research_progress.source_confidence_semantics: Heuristic research-source confidence only: official GOV.UK/PINS/HSE/Environment Agency/Natural England/Forestry Commission/Planning Data authority; current 2026 update/collector state where present, legal/process separation, authoritative-vs-MHCLG/partial/zero-data provenance, mapped-vs-exact-parcel controls and proposal-specific safety/water/ecology gates. Not parcel-level accuracy.

official_sources.name: Public Rights of Way & Common Land collection
official_sources.fact: PINS collection updated 21 January 2026 groups current common-land and public-rights-of-way guidance, forms, notices and decisions.
official_sources.gate: Collection availability is process guidance, not proof of the legal route, common-land status or definitive-map alignment for an exact parcel.

official_sources.name: Rights of way order decisions and maps published in 2026
official_sources.fact: PINS publishes 2026 rights-of-way order decisions and maps by authority; page updated 22 June 2026.
official_sources.gate: A published order decision elsewhere cannot be transferred to a target parcel; exact authority, order, status and map must match.

official_sources.name: Rights of way guidance booklet
official_sources.fact: PINS guidance updated 22 April 2026 covers objections, hearings, inquiries, decisions, modifications, costs and challenges.
official_sources.gate: Order procedure is separate from planning permission and does not establish that a path has been legally diverted or extinguished.

official_sources.name: Public rights of way: landowner responsibilities
official_sources.fact: Government guidance keeps route usability and legal creation/extinguishment/diversion processes separate.
official_sources.gate: A development layout or informal alternative route does not itself alter the legal public right of way.

official_sources.name: Planning Data public rights of way research
official_sources.fact: Planning Data research records partial multi-authority PRoW availability and separate diversion process where needed.
official_sources.gate: Research-stage/partial data is not a national authoritative definitive map and must not be used as exact parcel truth.

official_sources.name: Planning Data common land and village green dataset
official_sources.fact: Platform reports 0 records, 0 providers and no collection attempt; placeholder provenance is MHCLG-created.
official_sources.gate: Zero platform records means NO_DATA, not proof that a parcel is outside registered common land or a village green.

official_sources.name: Protected Landscapes duty guidance
official_sources.fact: Government guidance explains the strengthened duty affecting National Parks, National Landscapes and the Broads.
official_sources.gate: The duty is a decision-making obligation and does not by itself determine planning permission or exact parcel boundary status.

official_sources.name: Management plans for Protected Landscapes in England
official_sources.fact: Defra/Natural England guidance describes management-plan vision and strategy for protected landscapes.
official_sources.gate: A management plan is strategic context, not an automatic parcel refusal, permission or exact development-capacity result.

official_sources.name: Planning Data area of outstanding natural beauty dataset
official_sources.fact: Platform reports 34 AONB/National Landscape geographies from authoritative sources; collector ran 22 July 2026.
official_sources.gate: Designation geometry still must be intersected with exact canonical parcel geometry; designation alone does not determine permission.

official_sources.name: Planning Data national park dataset
official_sources.fact: Platform reports 10 national-park administrative boundaries for statistics; collector ran 23 July 2026 and mixed provenance is noted.
official_sources.gate: An administrative/statistical boundary must not be assumed to be the sole legally determinative protected-landscape boundary for parcel scoring.

official_sources.name: Planning Data national park authority dataset
official_sources.fact: Platform lists 10 national park authorities including the Broads and notes mixed provenance.
official_sources.gate: Authority identity or jurisdiction does not prove an exact parcel lies in a National Park or that a proposal is acceptable.

official_sources.name: Planning Data heritage coast dataset
official_sources.fact: Platform reports 32 heritage-coast geographies and notes some MHCLG-created data pending authoritative replacement.
official_sources.gate: Platform geometry is screening context; exact current boundary and local policy evidence remain required.

official_sources.name: Ancient woodland, ancient trees and veteran trees standing advice
official_sources.fact: Natural England and Forestry Commission standing advice identifies ancient woodland as irreplaceable habitat and sets an avoid-mitigate-compensate-last-resort framework.
official_sources.gate: Standing advice or proximity alone does not establish impact significance; exact habitat, buffers and proposal effects are needed.

official_sources.name: Planning Data ancient woodland dataset
official_sources.fact: Platform reports 44,373 ancient woodlands from an authoritative Natural England source; collector ran 22 July 2026.
official_sources.gate: Dataset overlap is a strong constraint signal but still requires exact parcel intersection and proposal-specific impact assessment.

official_sources.name: Planning Data site of special scientific interest dataset
official_sources.fact: Platform reports 4,128 SSSIs; collector ran 23 July 2026 and some MHCLG-created data is noted.
official_sources.gate: Platform overlap must be checked against current Natural England designation and consultation evidence before parcel scoring.

official_sources.name: Planning Data local nature reserve dataset
official_sources.fact: Platform reports 1,727 local nature reserves from two providers; collector ran 8 July 2026 with mixed provenance noted.
official_sources.gate: LNR presence is a planning constraint input, not proof of development prohibition or exact ecological effect.

official_sources.name: Planning Data special area of conservation dataset
official_sources.fact: Platform reports 260 SAC geographies; collector ran 18 July 2026 and some MHCLG-created data is noted.
official_sources.gate: SAC intersection is not a completed Habitats Regulations Assessment; exact features, pathways and mitigation must be assessed.

official_sources.name: Hazardous substances planning guidance
official_sources.fact: Planning Practice Guidance separates hazardous-substances consent, plan-making and nearby development controls.
official_sources.gate: Hazardous-substances consent does not replace planning permission, environmental permits or health-and-safety controls.

official_sources.name: HSE hazardous substances consent
official_sources.fact: HSE states controlled substances at or above defined limits require hazardous-substances consent and HSE is a statutory consultee.
official_sources.gate: Presence of a hazardous site or HSE consultation does not itself mean consent exists or nearby development must be refused.

official_sources.name: HSE land-use planning role
official_sources.fact: HSE sets consultation distances around major hazard sites and major accident hazard pipelines and advises on relevant developments.
official_sources.gate: Being inside a consultation distance is not an automatic refusal; exact zone, development type, scale and advice must be resolved.

official_sources.name: HSE land-use planning methodology
official_sources.fact: HSE methodology uses inner, middle and outer zones plus development sensitivity/type and scale to derive advice.
official_sources.gate: A map-zone hit alone cannot be converted into HSE advice without the relevant development type, scale and rule set.

official_sources.name: HSE Planning Advice Web App
official_sources.fact: HSE web app combines proximity zone with development type, size and intensity to produce advice.
official_sources.gate: A generic hazard layer is not a substitute for proposal-specific HSE Web App advice.

official_sources.name: HSE environmental impact assessment consultations
official_sources.fact: HSE explains EIA can require assessment of significant effects from vulnerability to major accidents and focuses on land-use-planning hazard controls.
official_sources.gate: EIA consultation is not hazardous-substances consent, HSE safety approval or planning permission.

official_sources.name: HSE developers planning application advice
official_sources.fact: HSE offers checks for consultation-zone location and, where applicable, an indication of HSE advice.
official_sources.gate: Pre-application advice is not the planning authority decision and can depend on exact proposal details.

official_sources.name: River basin management plans updated 2022
official_sources.fact: Environment Agency says current RBMPs set legally binding locally specific environmental objectives underpinning water regulation and planning.
official_sources.gate: RBMP objectives are strategic/legal context, not a parcel-specific WFD compliance result or permit.

official_sources.name: PINS Water Framework Directive advice for NSIPs
official_sources.fact: PINS advice updated 14 July 2026 describes WFD screening, scoping and impact-assessment stages and links with EIA/HRA.
official_sources.gate: Screening or scoping does not establish compliance; water-body identification, deterioration tests and project impacts remain required.

official_sources.name: RBMP current condition and environmental objectives
official_sources.fact: Current RBMP material covers condition, objectives, prevention of deterioration, protected areas and water-body status objectives.
official_sources.gate: A regional water-body objective is not a measured site discharge impact or evidence that a development can meet permitting requirements.

official_sources.name: RBMP implementing the plans
official_sources.fact: Environment Agency says public bodies must have due regard to the relevant RBMP when activities can affect a river basin district.
official_sources.gate: Due-regard duty does not itself confirm project compliance, mitigation delivery or permit grant.

official_sources.name: Water resources planning guideline
official_sources.fact: Guideline updated 16 June 2026 sets secure sustainable supply planning, forecasts, uncertainty and best-value options.
official_sources.gate: Company/regional planning does not prove connection capacity, abstraction availability or deliverability for an exact parcel.

official_sources.name: Planning Data HS2 safeguarded area dataset
official_sources.fact: Platform reports 0 records, 0 providers and no collection attempt, with MHCLG-created placeholder provenance.
official_sources.gate: Zero rows means NO_DATA and must not be interpreted as proof that a parcel is outside HS2 safeguarding directions.

official_sources.name: Planning Data safeguarded aerodrome dataset
official_sources.fact: Platform reports 0 safeguarded-aerodrome records, 0 providers and no collection attempt.
official_sources.gate: Zero rows means NO_DATA; authoritative aerodrome safeguarding/consultation evidence is still required where relevant.

official_sources.name: Planning Data safeguarded military explosives site dataset
official_sources.fact: Platform reports 0 safeguarded military-explosives-site records, 0 providers and no collection attempt.
official_sources.gate: Absence from the platform cannot be treated as absence of safeguarding or consultation constraints.

official_sources.name: Planning Data safeguarded wharf dataset
official_sources.fact: Platform reports 0 safeguarded-wharf records, 0 providers and no collection attempt.
official_sources.gate: Zero platform rows are a data-gap signal, not evidence that no safeguarded wharf policy affects a site.
